  \caption{\textbf{Structural audit of $1{,}000$ RefSeq bacterial genomes.} Rows for the six published predictors are recomputed from their per-genome prediction files with the score cut-offs of the original audit; every metric reproduces the audit's per-genome matrices. Essential completeness is the presence of the 22 core and 32 full essential GO terms in the propagated annotation (GO release 2025-03-16); complex coherence is the percentage of complex terms carried by at least two proteins; MetaCyc completeness is the percentage of annotated pathways with a complete EC combination; \texttt{has\_part} coherence is $100$ minus the percentage of missing \texttt{has\_part}-required terms. Taxon violations count protein--term rows whose term is forbidden for the genome's lineage (propagated rows, leaf rows, and proteins with at least one violation). GSPA rows are Stage 0 pooling and Stage 1 + 2A relaxation of DIAMOND, Pfam, and the audit\textquotesingle s own InterProScan claims at posterior $\ge 0.50$, run on all $1{,}000$ genomes with the operons of their RefSeq GFF3 and without gapseq gaps; the taxon-violating rows that remain after Stage 2A are terms forbidden by the audit\textquotesingle s constraint table but absent from the taxon table bundled with GSPA, whose own consistency check reports zero violations on every genome. GSPA ran in $268$~s (Stage 0) and $308$~s (Stage 1 + 2A) of wall time per genome on four cores, with InterProScan reused and untimed. Experimental GO truth covers $0.13$ proteins per genome on average, so no CAFA $F_{\max}$ or $S_{\min}$ is reported; the original audit logged no runtime or memory. Source: \texttt{results/pillar1\_suite2\_1000bacteria\_sota.tsv} (pipeline P12).}
